title: How do you line up rotating arms from smallest to largest?
description: Rotating arms are made from two paper straws and a paper clip. Two arms are compared with their joints together and one straw along one straw, and the arms are lined up in order. Keeko's doubt is that arms can be compared by eye wherever they lie.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare two angles with the joints together and one straw along one straw. Watch for the slip of comparing the arms by eye anywhere on the table.

source: Make several 'rotating arms' (two paper straws and a paper c
video_script.why: The child makes rotating arms and lines them up by laying them over each other.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rotating arms made of two paper straws and a paper clip
video_script.anchor: two paper straws joined by a paper clip to make a rotating arm
video_script.wrong_answer: we can lay the arms anywhere on the table and compare by eye
video_script.wrong_move: compares arms that lie at different places and point different ways
video_script.payoff_line: Compare with the joints together, then line the arms up from smallest to largest

final_answer.value: place the arms over each other with the joints together, compare the openings, and arrange them in order
final_answer.spoken: place the arms over each other with the joints together, compare the openings, and arrange them in order

hold_back: line the arms up from smallest
maths_rules: rotating arm: two straws pushed into a paper clip; the opening between the straws is the angle
compare two arms: joints together, one straw along one straw, then see where the second straw falls
the arm whose second straw falls farther out has the larger opening
repeat for neighbouring arms and arrange the arms from smallest to largest
slip: arms lying at different places and turned different ways cannot be compared fairly by eye
video_script.design: One idea: compare with the joints together, then arrange in order. The rotating arm stays on the board. Keeko's doubt: lay the arms anywhere and compare by eye.
